caption: Repeater-lock D latch, 4 blocks (track memory census): the data input feeds repeater M (on stone) whose output is q; the enable input feeds a second repeater L pointing into M's side. While L is on M is locked and holds q; while it is off M follows d. Transparent while e is OFF (`enable low`), latency 4 gt.

Dropper RS latch, 4 blocks (track memory): droppers A (facing east) and B (facing west) face each other and hold one stone. s (next to A) fires A and the stone goes to B; r (next to B) fires B and it comes back; firing the empty one does nothing, so repeated s or r change nothing. A comparator on stone reads B: q is its output (1). Latency 6 gt (dropper 4 + comparator 2).

D latch, enable high, 5 blocks (track memory): repeater M carries d to q; comparator C in subtract mode points into M's side, with a redstone block behind it (15) and the enable input at its side, so C gives 15 - e: M is locked (holds q) while e is off and follows d while e is on. Latency 4 gt.

Counter 3, dropper corner ring, 8 blocks (track memory): the input cell touches three droppers on three axes (east, up, south); between each pair a hopper carries the stone on to the next dropper (dropper up -> hopper west -> dropper south -> hopper down -> dropper east -> hopper north). Each pulse fires all three; only the one holding the stone moves it, and its hopper delivers it after all three have fired, so the stone advances one dropper per pulse whatever the firing order. The comparator reads the east dropper: on during one pulse window in three (level style).
Counter 2, one copper bulb, 3 blocks (track memory): the copper bulb T flip-flop seen as a counter: the input toggles the bulb, its comparator's level alternates every pulse (level style, period 2).

Counter 2 as a divider, two copper bulbs, 6 blocks (track memory): the input toggles bulb 1, its comparator toggles bulb 2 on every second pulse; bulb 2's comparator changes state once every two pulses and holds between (toggles style).

Counter 4, two copper bulbs, 6 blocks (track memory): the input toggles bulb 1, its comparator toggles bulb 2 on every second pulse, and bulb 2's comparator is the output: on for two pulse windows, off for two (level style, period 4; the same build divides by 2 as a toggle stream).

Counter 8, three copper bulbs, 9 blocks (track memory): a chain of three bulb T flip-flops (bulb + comparator each), each comparator toggling the next bulb; the last comparator is on for four pulse windows and off for four (level style, period 8).

Counter 6, dropper corner ring + copper bulb, 11 blocks (track memory): the counter3-corner ring (the input cell touches three droppers; hoppers pass the stone one dropper per pulse) lights its comparator one window in three; that comparator toggles a copper bulb, read by a second comparator: on for three pulse windows, off for three (level style, period 6; as a toggle stream it divides by 3).

Counter 5, dropper star ring, 12 blocks (track memory): the input cell touches five droppers (east, south, west, north, up); five hoppers on the edges between them close a ring east -> south -> west -> north -> up -> east (dropper, hopper, dropper, ...). Each pulse fires all five droppers; only the one holding the stone moves it, and its hopper delivers it to the next dropper after all have fired, so the stone advances one dropper per pulse whatever the firing order. The comparator reads the east dropper: on during one pulse window in five (level style).

Counter 4, dropper ring around the input, 10 blocks (track memory): the input cell touches four droppers (east, south, west, north); four hoppers in the corners close a ring east -> south -> west -> north -> east (dropper, hopper, dropper, ...). Each pulse fires all four; the dropper holding the stone moves it into its hopper, which delivers it to the next dropper after all have fired, so the stone advances one dropper per pulse. The comparator reads the east dropper: on during one pulse window in four (level style).

Crafter RS latch, 6 blocks (track memory): crafter A (nine iron ingots, next to s) faces a hopper that feeds crafter B (next to r), which faces a hopper that feeds A. s makes A craft an iron block, carried into B; r makes B craft nine ingots, carried back into A (one per 8 gt, spread over its nine slots). Firing an empty crafter does nothing, so repeated s or r change nothing. A comparator reads B: 1 with the block, 0 without.

Counter 2, dropper ring, 8 blocks (track memory, `mctas circuit memory ring --n 2`): the input cell fires 2 droppers (0 next to it, 2 through 2 dust), and 2 hoppers between them close the cycle dropper -> hopper -> dropper; each pulse fires every dropper, only the one holding the stone moves it, and its hopper delivers it to the next dropper after all have fired, so the stone advances one dropper per pulse whatever the firing order. The comparator reads one dropper: on during one pulse window in 2 (level style).
